source.title: MENTIS: What Belief Changes Under Alignment? Measuring Multi-Scale Latent Torsion in Language Models
source.authors: Partha Pratim Saha; Samarth Raina; Mayur Parvatikar; Amit Dhanda; Vinija Jain; Aman Chadha; Amitava Das

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses shallow safety alignment and refusal, but its own measurements are of hidden-state torsion. It does not test the claim versions’ refusal behavior, response-position KL, bypass interventions, parameter localization, causes of shallowness, or deepening methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports geometric alignment measurements on safe and unsafe prompts, but torsion is not a measure of refusal/compliance, per-token KL, or bypass success. These results are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. Cited claims about shallow safety and refusal directions are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: All results are hidden-state torsion between paired IT and PA checkpoints on LITMUS prompts. There are no refusal or harmful-compliance rates, no fine-tuning attacks, no per-token KL across response positions, no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, no parameter localization tied to safety behaviour, and no deepening training. Section 3.5 argues that a 'shallow-refusal account' would predict larger shifts on unsafe prompts and reports the opposite. But torsion across transformer layers, read out at only the first gold-response token, does not measure what V3 names (per-token KL across response positions), nor does it measure safety behaviour. So this is a related construct, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Add that the authors explicitly present the safe-prompt result as moving beyond 'shallow safety filter' or refusal-only accounts of alignment, while calling the work diagnostic, not causal.
record.recipe_differences: Paired-checkpoint geometric measurement of hidden-state torsion; no harmful or benign fine-tuning intervention, per-token KL measurement, or bypass intervention from the claim’s original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported torsion peak depth varies by architecture. Safe-versus-unsafe torsion magnitudes also differ across model pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Safe prompts show larger IT→PA torsion shifts than unsafe prompts in all four pairs. The authors frame this as evidence against a refusal-only or shallow-filter view of alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference alignment changes internal layerwise geometry more for safe than for unsafe prompts, measured at the first response token.

fits_no_version.finding: Normative concepts show larger aggregate T1 shifts than factual concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment-induced internal geometric change is concept-selective.

fits_no_version.finding: The ERA torsion peak lies at architecture-specific layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth of peak alignment-induced torsion varies by model family.

fits_no_version.finding: Torsion is negatively correlated with contextual entropy for WAR in OLMo and Mistral.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment-related torsion is lower in higher-entropy contexts.

record.problems: The study is descriptive and does not causally validate the geometric changes. It uses LITMUS and 7–8B decoder-only models; prompt-level observations may not be independent. The paper notes small absolute torsion shifts and dependence on readout, target-token, and benchmark choices. It reports no refusal-rate or harmful-completion tests relevant to the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only per-concept profiles and qualitative examples were not extracted because the text does not give their individual numerical values. Comparisons of MENTIS with CKA, cosine distance, and RepE were left out because they do not measure the claim versions’ named behaviors or mechanisms.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions; only the first gold-response token is used as a readout.
Whether safety behaviour is carried by a small set of weights or ranks. The ERA layer peaks concern torsion, not safety behaviour, and have no causal test.
Data or objective causes of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix M is internally inconsistent: the Mistral and Llama 'IT and PA' pairs are listed as the same single Instruct checkpoint, and Tülu has no ids. This conflicts with the stated same-model null (Δτ < 1e-4) and undermines R3, R5, R6, R10 and R11. The entropy claim (Section 3.3) conflicts with Figure 12 and Appendix I (ρ = −0.18, p = 0.50). The anti-shallow-alignment argument rests on layer-depth geometry, not response-position measures, so it does not bear on V3 as stated.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance or refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance or refusal.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Compliant-prefix prefilling, suffix attacks, or decoding changes and their effect on harmful completion.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety behavior and whether the result persists.

rows.subject: four 7–8B IT→PA model pairs (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Instruction-Tuned to Preference-Aligned; DPO- or RLHF-style
rows.operation_detail: Compared category-level T1 torsion shifts between IT and PA checkpoints.
rows.note: Category-level result; the text does not provide separate values for each model pair. Torsion is an internal geometric measure, not a safety-behavior rate.

rows.subject: OLMo-2-1124-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the association between contextual entropy and T1 torsion.

conditions.value: Spearman correlation of τT1 and contextual entropy

rows.measure: Spearman ρ between torsion and contextual entropy
rows.note: Reported as the entropy–torsion relationship for WAR; this is not a response-position KL measurement.
rows.check: Section 3.3 reports a negative entropy-torsion correlation. Figure 12 and Appendix I report ρ = −0.18, p = 0.50 at concept and word level, which conflicts with the 'statistically reliable' framing. The value matches the text.
